summary: This Wikipedia article surveys how Mary, mother of Jesus, is treated across traditions. It covers her portrayal in the Qur'an, the Orthodox veneration of the Theotokos, Martin Luther's views on Marian devotion, Anglican feast days, and the infancy narratives in the Protoevangelium of James and the Gospels. It also notes Ephesus traditions and early polemics against the Virgin birth.
one_line: Overview of Mary, mother of Jesus, as portrayed in the Qur'an, Orthodox and Anglican traditions, Martin Luther's views, and apocryphal and biblical accounts.
key_facts: The Qur'an relates detailed narrative accounts of Maryam (Mary) in Qur'an 3:35–47 and 19:16–34.
The account in Sura 19 is nearly identical with that in the Gospel according to Luke.
Orthodox Christianity holds that Mary was and remained a virgin before and after Christ's birth, and she is called the Theotokos.
Within the Orthodox order of saints, the Theotokos comes first, followed by Angels, Prophets, Apostles, Fathers and Martyrs; she is proclaimed the "Lady of the Angels".
Theologians appear to agree that Martin Luther adhered to the Marian decrees of the ecumenical councils and held that Mary was a perpetual virgin and the Theotokos.
Luther considered the Roman Catholic practice of celebrating saints' days and making intercessory requests to Mary and departed saints to be idolatry.
Pope Pius IX dogmatized the Immaculate Conception in 1854.
All member churches of the Anglican Communion affirm in the historic creeds that Jesus was born of the Virgin Mary.
Anglicans observe the Annunciation on March 25, the Visitation on 31 May (or July 2 in some provinces), the Assumption feast on August 15, and the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin on September 8.
The Protoevangelium of James says Mary was consecrated as a virgin at the temple at age three and was miraculously fed by an angel until she was twelve.
Sergei Bulgakov wrote: "The Virgin Mary is the center, invisible, but real, of the Apostolic Church."
In the 19th century, a house near Ephesus in Turkey was found based on the visions of Anne Catherine Emmerich, an Augustinian nun in Germany.
Irenaeus and Eusebius of Caesarea wrote that John later went to Ephesus, which may underlie the belief that Mary also lived in Ephesus with John.
According to the apocryphal Gospel of James, Mary was the daughter of Saint Joachim and Saint Anne.
Mary resided in Nazareth in Galilee, and during her betrothal the angel Gabriel announced she would conceive the Messiah through the Holy Spirit.
In the 2nd century, Celsus suggested Jesus was the illegitimate son of a Roman soldier named Panthera; Origen considered this a fabricated story.

entities.name: Mary (Maryam)
entities.role: Mother of Jesus, the central figure of the article, venerated as the Theotokos and recounted in the Qur'an and Gospels

entities.name: Qur'an
entities.role: Source of detailed narrative accounts of Maryam in suras 3 and 19

entities.name: Gospel according to Luke
entities.role: Gospel whose account is nearly identical with Sura 19 and which begins with the visitation to Zakariya and the annunciation

entities.name: Zakariya (Zecharias)
entities.role: Figure visited by an angel, with the Good News of the birth of Yahya (John) given to him

entities.name: Martin Luther
entities.role: Reformer whose views on Mary, the Immaculate Conception, the Assumption and saints' veneration are discussed

entities.name: Pope Pius IX
entities.role: Pope who dogmatized the Immaculate Conception in 1854

entities.name: Sergei Bulgakov
entities.role: Orthodox theologian who wrote that the Virgin Mary is the center of the Apostolic Church

entities.name: Anglican Communion
entities.role: Church whose member churches affirm the Virgin birth and observe Marian feast days

entities.name: Protoevangelium of James
entities.role: Extra-canonical book that is the source of many Orthodox beliefs about Mary, including her temple consecration

entities.name: Anne Catherine Emmerich
entities.role: Augustinian nun in Germany whose visions led to the discovery of a house near Ephesus

entities.name: Ephesus
entities.role: City in Turkey where a house identified as the House of the Virgin Mary was found

entities.name: John the Evangelist
entities.role: Disciple whom Jesus loved, with whom Mary went to live according to the Gospel of John

entities.name: Irenaeus
entities.role: Writer whose history records that John later went to Ephesus

entities.name: Eusebius of Caesarea
entities.role: Writer whose history records that John later went to Ephesus

entities.name: Saint Joachim
entities.role: Father of Mary according to the apocryphal Gospel of James

entities.name: Saint Anne
entities.role: Mother of Mary according to the apocryphal Gospel of James

entities.name: Nazareth in Galilee
entities.role: Town where Mary resided in her own house

entities.name: Gabriel
entities.role: Angel who announced to Mary that she would be the mother of the promised Messiah

entities.name: Joseph
entities.role: Mary's husband, who was told of her conception in a dream and took her as his wife

entities.name: Celsus
entities.role: Early anti-Christian polemicist who suggested Jesus was the illegitimate son of a Roman soldier named Panthera

entities.name: Origen
entities.role: Church Father in Alexandria, Egypt, who responded to Celsus and considered the story fabricated
